'''Gregory James Brown III''' (born September 1, 2001) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[AEK B.C.|AEK Athens]] of the [[Greek Basketball League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas Longhorns]].

==Early life==
Brown grew up playing basketball under the guidance of his uncle, [[Roderick Anderson]], a former professional basketball player.<ref name="clynch">{{cite web |last=Clynch |first=Shawn |title=A U.T. basketball great mentoring a rising star |url=https://www.kvue.com/article/sports/a-ut-basketball-great-mentoring-a-rising-star/301100881 |publisher=[[KVUE (Texas)|KVUE]] |accessdate=April 22, 2020 |date=August 17, 2016}}</ref> Brown attended [[Vandegrift High School]] in [[Austin, Texas]], where he was a four-year [[varsity team|varsity]] basketball starter, in addition to competing in varsity [[track and field]] in the [[high jump]]. As a freshman, he recorded his first [[triple-double]] with 15 points, 14 rebounds and a school-record 18 blocks in a win over [[Hutto High School]].<ref name="riggs">{{cite web |last=Riggs |first=Randy |title=Vandegrift freshman Brown III soaring to statistical heights |url=https://www.statesman.com/NEWS/20170111/Vandegrift-freshman-Brown-III-soaring-to-statistical-heights |website=[[Austin American-Statesman]] |accessdate=April 22, 2020 |date=January 11, 2017}}</ref> In his freshman season, Brown averaged 17.2 points, 10.7 rebounds and 3.6 blocks per game, earning All-Central Texas Newcomer of the Year honors from the ''[[Austin American-Statesman]]''.<ref name="field">{{cite web |last=Field |first=Carson |title=Brown looks to shine in second season at Vandegrift |url=https://www.fourpointsnews.com/2017/10/20/brown-looks-shine-second-season-vandegrift/ |publisher=Four Points News |accessdate=April 22, 2020 |date=October 20, 2017}}</ref>

As a sophomore, Brown averaged 27.4 points, 12.3 rebounds, and 2.5 blocks per game en route to District 25-6A offensive [[most valuable player]] (MVP) accolades. He led the district in scoring and rebounding.<ref name="wells">{{cite web |last=Wells |first=Justin |title=One-on-One with 5-star Greg Brown III |url=https://insidetexas.com/one-on-one-with-5-star-greg-brown-iii/ |publisher=Inside Texas |accessdate=April 22, 2020 |date=March 15, 2018}}</ref> In his junior season, Brown averaged 30.1 points, 13.5 rebounds and 5.4 blocks per game. He missed 14 games early in the season with a dislocated finger. Brown was named to the All-Central Texas first team for his third straight year.<ref name="bils">{{cite web |last=Bils |first=Chris |title='Highlight reel' Greg Brown III happy to carry a heavy load for Vandegrift |url=https://www.statesman.com/sports/20190328/highlight-reel-greg-brown-iii-happy-to-carry-heavy-load-for-vandegrift |website=[[Austin American-Statesman]] |accessdate=April 22, 2020 |date=March 28, 2019}}</ref> As a senior, he averaged 26.1 points, 13.2 rebounds and 3.5 blocks per game, collecting District 13-6A MVP, Texas [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]] and ''Austin American-Statesman'' All-Central Texas Player of the Year honors. Brown led Vandegrift to a program-best 33–3 record and its first district title. He was selected to play in the [[2020 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American Game]], which was canceled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Jordan |first=Jason |title=McDonald's All American Game Cancelled Amid COVID-19 Concerns |url=https://www.si.com/college/recruiting/basketball/mcdonalds-all-american-covid19-coronavirus-ncaa-tournament |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |accessdate=March 30, 2020 |date=March 12, 2019}}</ref><ref name="jones">{{cite web |last=Jones |first=Thomas |title=Greg Brown III leads honors in District 13-6A boys basketball |url=https://www.alicetx.com/sports/20200330/greg-brown-iii-leads-honors-in-district-13-6a-boys-basketball |website=[[Alice Echo-News Journal]] |accessdate=April 22, 2020 |date=March 30, 2020}}</ref><ref name="hamilton">{{cite web |last=Hamilton |first=Brian |title=Greg Brown could remain Austin's hometown hero, but the top recruit has options |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1738044/2020/04/13/greg-brown-could-remain-austins-hometown-hero-but-the-top-recruit-has-options/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=April 22, 2020 |date=April 13, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Jones |first=Thomas |title=All-Central Texas boys basketball team: Vandegrift star Greg Brown III adds to honors |url=https://www.statesman.com/sports/20200409/all-central-texas-boys-basketball-team-vandegrift-star-greg-brown-iii-adds-to-honors |accessdate=April 22, 2020 |work=[[Austin American-Statesman]] |date=April 9, 2020}}</ref>

Brown drew the attention of major [[college basketball]] programs before high school.<ref name=clynch/> In his freshman year, he emerged as one of the best players in the 2020 class and held basketball offers from several schools, including [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] and [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]].<ref name=field/> By the end of his high school career, Brown was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and a top-10 player in the 2020 class, according to major recruiting services. He trimmed his offers to [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]], [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]], [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]] or Texas, or opt to instead play professionally.<ref name="howe">{{cite web |last=Howe |first=Jeff |title=Going pro an option for five-star Texas target Greg Brown |url=https://247sports.com/college/texas/Article/Greg-Brown-III-college-basketball-recruiting-G-League-option-April-24-decision-Texas-Longhorns-146146085/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |accessdate=April 22, 2020 |date=April 16, 2020}}</ref> On April 24, 2020, he announced his commitment to Texas over Auburn, Memphis, Michigan, Kentucky and a $300,000 offer from the [[G League]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Spears |first=Marc J. |date=April 24, 2020 |title=All-American Greg Brown III commits to play for the Texas Longhorns |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29094836 |accessdate=April 26, 2020 |publisher=[[ESPN]]}}</ref>

==College career==
In his college debut on November 25, 2020, Brown recorded 11 points and 10 rebounds in a 91–55 win against [[2020–21 Texas–Rio Grande Valley Vaqueros men's basketball team|Texas–Rio Grande Valley]].<ref>{{cite news |title=No. 19 Texas opens with 91–55 win over Rio Grande Valley |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401254076 |access-date=November 30, 2020 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 25, 2020}}</ref> On December 20, he posted a career-high 24 points, 14 rebounds and three blocks in a 77–74 win over [[2020–21 Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball team|Oklahoma State]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Davis |first=Brian |title=Texas 77, Oklahoma State 74: Greg Brown's season starting to take full flight |url=https://www.hookem.com/story/sports/mens-basketball/2020/12/20/texas-greg-brown-pure-dynamite-vs-oklahoma-state/3985921001/ |website=Hookem |access-date=July 22, 2021 |date=December 20, 2020}}</ref> As a freshman, Brown averaged 9.3 points and 6.2 rebounds per game. He earned All-[[Big 12]] honorable mention and was an All-Freshman Team and All-Newcomer Team selection. On May 13, 2021, Brown declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.<ref>{{cite web |last=Conway |first=Tyler |title=Texas' Greg Brown Declares for 2021 NBA Draft, Signs with Agent |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2933384-texas-greg-brown-declares-for-2021-nba-draft-signs-with-agent |website=[[Bleacher Report]] |access-date=July 22, 2021 |date=May 13, 2021}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Portland Trail Blazers (2021–2023)===
Brown was selected in the second round of the [[2021 NBA draft]] with the 43rd pick by the [[New Orleans Pelicans]]. He was then traded to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]<ref>{{cite news |last=Yohannes |first=Aron |title=Portland Trail Blazers make trade, select Greg Brown from Texas: 3 things to know |url=https://www.oregonlive.com/blazers/2021/07/portland-trail-blazers-make-trade-select-greg-brown-from-texas-3-things-to-know.html |access-date=August 2, 2021 |work=[[The Oregonian]] |date=July 29, 2021}}</ref> for a future second-round draft pick and cash considerations.<ref>{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers acquire draft rights to Greg Brown III|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/2021/7/29/trail-blazers-acquire-draft-rights-to-greg-brown-iii|date=July 29, 2021|publisher=National Basketball Association|accessdate=July 29, 2021}}</ref> Brown joined the Trail Blazers for the [[2021 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 3, 2021 |title=Trail Blazers Announce 2021 NBA Summer League Roster |url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/2021/8/3/trail-blazers-announce-2021-nba-summer-league-roster |access-date=March 27, 2022 |publisher=National Basketball Association}}</ref> On August 12, 2021, he signed a 3-year, $4.3 million rookie scale contract with the Trail Blazers.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 12, 2021 |title=Trail Blazers Sign Greg Brown III |url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/story/2021/8/12/trail-blazers-sign-greg-brown-iii |access-date=March 27, 2022 |publisher=National Basketball Association}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Trail Blazers sign 2nd-round rookie Greg Brown III using the TMLE |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/northwest/trail-blazers/trail-blazers-sign-2nd-round-rookie-greg-brown-iii-using-tmle |access-date=March 27, 2022 |website=NBC Sports |archive-date=September 17, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210917005115/https://www.nbcsports.com/northwest/trail-blazers/trail-blazers-sign-2nd-round-rookie-greg-brown-iii-using-tmle |url-status=dead }}</ref> On October 23, Brown made his NBA debut, logging four points and three rebounds in a 134–105 blowout win over the [[Phoenix Suns]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gundersen |first=Erik García |date=October 24, 2021 |title=Phoenix Suns vs Portland Trail Blazers Oct 23, 2021 Game Summary |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100033 |access-date=March 27, 2022 |publisher=National Basketball Association}}</ref> On February 8, 2022, he scored a season-high 15 points, along with eight rebounds, in a 95–113 loss to the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 9, 2022 |title=Magic down Blazers 113-95 after Portland deals away McCollum |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401360642 |access-date=March 27, 2022 |publisher=ESPN}}</ref> On March 23, in a 96–133 blowout loss to the [[San Antonio Spurs]], Brown grabbed a season-high 14 rebounds, along with seven points and two blocks.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 24, 2022 |title=Murray has 28 points, Spurs rout Trail Blazers 133-96 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401360913 |access-date=March 27, 2022 |publisher=ESPN}}</ref>

On February 9, 2023, Brown was waived by the Blazers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Deckard |first=Dave |date=February 9, 2023 |title=Trail Blazers Waive Greg Brown III |url=https://www.blazersedge.com/2023/2/9/23593245/trail-blazers-waive-greg-brown-iii-nba-trade-deadline-2023-stats-2021-draft |access-date=February 9, 2023 |website=SBNation.com}}</ref>

===San Diego Clippers (2023)===
On March 2, 2023, Brown was acquired by the [[Ontario Clippers]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Rory|last=Maher|title=Greg Brown Signs With Ontario Clippers|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2023/03/greg-brown-signs-with-ontario-clippers.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=March 2, 2023|access-date=March 2, 2023}}</ref>

===Dallas Mavericks (2023–2024)===
On August 14, 2023, Brown signed with the [[Dallas Mavericks]]<ref>{{cite web|first=Eddie|last=Sefko|title=Mavericks sign three, including Fall Classic alumnus|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavs-sign-three|website=Mavs.com|date=August 14, 2023|access-date=August 15, 2023}}</ref> and on October 21, his deal was converted into a [[two-way contract]].<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Mavs PR|title=The Dallas Mavericks have converted Dexter Dennis and Greg Brown III to Two-Way contracts. Dennis will wear #17. Brown III will wear #13.|number=1715805207219655029|user=MavsPR|date=October 21, 2023|access-date=October 24, 2023}}</ref> Brown reached the [[2024 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]] where the Mavericks lost to the [[Boston Celtics]] in five games.<ref>{{cite web|title=Boston Celtics defeat Dallas Mavericks to win 2024 NBA Finals|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/boston-celtics-beat-dallas-mavericks-2024-nba-finals/|website=CBSNews.com|date=June 17, 2024|access-date=June 17, 2024}}</ref>

===Mexico City Capitanes (2024–2025)===
On October 28, 2024, Brown joined the [[Mexico City Capitanes]].<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Capitanes CDMX|title=Presentando roster para nuestro Training Camp 2024 ⬇️ #EstoEsCapitanes|number=1850907877126598762|user=CapitanesCDMX|date=October 28, 2024|access-date=October 29, 2024|language=Spanish}}</ref>

=== Calgary Surge (2025) ===
On April 2, 2025, Brown signed with the [[Calgary Surge]] of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball League]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=CALGARY SURGE SIGN FORMER NBA PLAYER GREG BROWN III, 6"7" FORWARD FROM AUSTIN, TEXAS |url=https://www.calgarysurge.ca/calgary-surge-sign-former-nba-player-greg-brown-iii-67-forward-from-austin-texas |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250402172013/https://www.calgarysurge.ca/calgary-surge-sign-former-nba-player-greg-brown-iii-67-forward-from-austin-texas |archive-date=April 2, 2025 |access-date=2025-06-12 |language=en |url-status=live }}</ref> Brown averaged 19.7 points, 8.2 and 1.8 blocks in 23 games played with Calgary. He was the runner-up for CEBL Defensive Player of the Year and was named a CEBL First Team All Star.<ref>{{Cite web |title=CEBL Stars Honoured in Winnipeg as 2025 Award Winners Revealed |date=August 22, 2025 |url=https://www.cebl.ca/cebl-stars-honoured-in-winnipeg-as-2025-award-winners-revealed}}</ref>

===AEK Athens (2025–present)===
On November 12, 2025, Brown III signed with [[AEK B.C.|AEK Athens]] of the [[Greek Basket League]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-11-12 |title=AEK signs former NBA player Greg Brown III |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/fiba-champions-league/1893596/aek-signs-greg-brown-iii-former-nba-player/ |access-date=2025-11-13 |website=Eurohoops |language=en}}</ref> On March 16, he extended his contract with the club until 2027.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-03-16 |title=AEK locks down Greg Brown III with long-term contract extension |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/fiba-champions-league/1944339/greg-brown-iii-signs-contract-extension-aek-basketball-champions-league/ |access-date=2026-03-20 |website=Eurohoops |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Brown's grandfather, Greg Brown, Sr., played wide receiver for Grambling from 1971 to 1974. His father, Greg Brown, Jr., played [[college football]] as a [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] for [[Texas Longhorns football|Texas]] before playing in the [[NFL Europe]], stints at camp and on the practice squads of the [[Denver Broncos]] and [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] of the [[National Football League]], with the [[Austin Wranglers]] of the [[Arena Football League]] and with the [[CenTex Barracudas]] of the [[Intense Football League]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Former Longhorn Greg Brown signs with Tampa Bay Buccaneers |url=https://texassports.com/news/2003/7/16/071603aaa_110.aspx |publisher=University of Texas Athletics |accessdate=April 22, 2020 |date=July 16, 2003}}</ref> 

Brown's uncle, [[Roderick Anderson]], played [[college basketball]] as a [[point guard]] for [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]] before playing professionally overseas.<ref name=clynch/>
